title: Eiffel Tower

when.label: 26 January 1887 – 31 March 1889
when.note: Construction dates as given by the tower's operator.

summary: The 300-metre iron tower was built in just over two years for the 1889 World's Fair in Paris, held on the centenary of the French Revolution.
description: The tower was chosen from 107 proposals in a competition for the Exposition Universelle of 1889. The winning design came from the entrepreneur Gustave Eiffel, the engineers Maurice Koechlin and Émile Nouguier, and the architect Stephen Sauvestre.
Digging began on 26 January 1887, and the tower was finished on 31 March 1889 — 2 years, 2 months and 5 days later. Its iron parts were joined with some 2,500,000 rivets.
context: Maurice Koechlin and Émile Nouguier, the two chief engineers in Eiffel's company, had the idea for a very tall tower in June 1884, and Eiffel registered a patent for the design that September. The 1889 fair marked the 100th anniversary of the French Revolution.
The banks of the Seine in Paris, including the Eiffel Tower, were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1991.

facts.text: Works began on 26 January 1887 and the tower was completed on 31 March 1889.
The design by Eiffel, Koechlin, Nouguier and Sauvestre was selected from 107 projects.
About 2,500,000 rivets were used; between 150 and 300 workers were on the construction site.
